title: Why bother with Steam?
author: Ashamed-Cost-5548
selftext: Why bother with Steam when they require AI disclosure? Epic and Tim Sweeney seem to champion AI maybe more AI dev should focus on selling their game on Epic.

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body:
Well, the principles are set by someone else, so I'm not too sure how I need to adhere to someone else's principles.

Outside of that, the AI-generated assets (about 30% of the assets) were all created by a model that was trained on my own art from the past two decades... so I seriously wonder how people could have any problems with that (outside of them just being oblivious...).

But no, I'd not call my two games revolutionary, but they're evolutionary in that they combine two different genres that I had not seen before.  
It just was the kind of game I wanted to play, so I built it. And I'm glad I did, as it has given me an enormous amount of freedom, and I'm currently working a leisurely 4-day workweek, where I decide what days I work... I'm fucking lucky, tbh.

replies.author: Don_Equis

> Do they?

Yes. On Steam they do. You have other channels for selling that doesn't force you to disclose it, and in those you would be in your total right to not do so. But not when the platform forces you.

So it is not a natural right that you have to disclose it. It is your obligation when using Steam.

comments.author: MessageSelfdestructs
comments.body:
I'm perfectly happy having given more than $160k of my profit to Steam: they've offered me a great platform with lots of users, and have great features for me as a developer.  
I'm also on Epic, but the sales on there (even with the lower percentage) can't even be compared in the slightest to the sales I'm getting on Steam: I'm more so on there for commercial reasons, so people get exposed to my game... so they can buy it on Steam. :-D

And outside of that, I've been an incredibly happy customer for more than 2 decades, and always admire how much they put me as a customer on the forefront.

And lastly, I think Gabe Newell is an awesome person, whereas Tim Sweeny is a megacunt (though admittedly, this doesn't play a great part in me loving Steam).
